clue.text: Poser in pub or on TV perhaps

definitions.text: Poser in pub or on TV perhaps

parts.words: Poser in pub or on TV perhaps
parts.note: a poser here is not someone striking attitudes but one who poses questions, at a pub quiz night or on a television game show

explanation.definitionFit: The host who puts questions to contestants at a pub quiz or on a TV show is literally a poser of questions.

clue.text: Unlikely Victor could be grounded after accident

indicators.note: after an accident things are broken and jumbled, signalling the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Victor, an unlikely pilot, could be grounded following a crash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after accident' rearranges GROUNDED; 'Victor' poses as a name but means winner.
explanation.definitionFit: An underdog is the competitor expected to lose, so its victory is unlikely.

clue.text: Quickly drive miles away and park

indicators.note: away means the letter for miles is sent off and removed

parts.note: to zoom is to drive very fast

explanation.surface: Speed off for miles and then pull up and park.
explanation.walkthrough: 'park' looks like a verb at the end of a driving sentence but is a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A zoo is a zoological park where animals are kept for viewing.

clue.text: Supervisor of brothers between 7 and 14 in the other set

indicators.note: only the stretch lying between, across the join of the two named entries, is kept; the rest of each is discarded

parts.note: for a down clue the other set is the across clues, so these are the across entries numbered 7 and 14, read one after the other

explanation.surface: A head of monks sits between numbered places in another group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the other set' means the across clues, as this is a down clue; the answer straddles the end of 7 across and the start of 14 across, AB plus BOT.
explanation.definitionFit: An abbot is the head of an abbey of monks, who address one another as brothers.

clue.text: State thus able to retain odd pieces of writing

parts.note: Tex. is an abbreviation for Texas, a US state

indicators.note: keeping only the odd pieces means keeping the first, third, fifth and seventh letters

explanation.surface: A state is so able that it hangs on to the odd scraps of writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to retain odd pieces' keeps letters 1, 3, 5 and 7 of THUS ABLE: T, U, A, L.
explanation.definitionFit: Textual means relating to a text, that is, to written words.

clue.text: Decay can almost totally beset old bit of tooth

indicators.note: to beset is to surround, so the old letter is enclosed

parts.note: rot is decay
taken as written

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: all means totally, wholly

explanation.surface: Tooth decay can almost entirely surround an old piece of a tooth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can' looks like a verb in the surface but is simply the letters CAN, part of the canal; 'almost' cuts the last letter from 'totally', and 'beset' encloses O.
explanation.definitionFit: The root canal is the channel inside a tooth's root that holds the pulp.

clue.text: Sign of over-indulgence following party

parts.note: F is the standard abbreviation for following, as in page references
Lab is short for the Labour Party, a British political party

explanation.surface: A paunch that appears after a night of partying.
explanation.definitionFit: Excess body fat is the visible evidence of eating and drinking too much.

clue.text: After mild oath I declined to see red

parts.note: flip is a mild exclamation of annoyance, as in flipping heck
I as a pronoun can be rendered one, as in one does
slid means went down, declined

explanation.surface: After a mild curse, I went downhill and lost my temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I' is the formal pronoun ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: To see red and to flip one's lid are both idioms for becoming furious.

clue.text: . Put up with lying about identity

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: lying abed means lying in bed
ID is short for identity, as in an ID card

explanation.surface: Someone tolerated lies told about who they were.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lying' suggests untruths but means lying down, ABED, which goes about ID.
explanation.definitionFit: To abide something is to tolerate it, so abided means put up with.

clue.text: Hit on ear with thick tube

parts.note: a thick person, a dullard, is an idiot
to box someone's ears is to hit them on the ear

explanation.surface: Someone cuffs another round the head with a stout pipe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thick' reads as an adjective for the tube but stands for a noun, a dimwit; 'tube' is slang for television.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal, slightly scornful names for the television set.

clue.text: Girl in love with passionate answer for Duke

parts.note: love is nil in tennis scoring, written as the round letter O

indicators.note: answer for Duke means the letter standing for answer takes the place of the one standing for Duke

parts.note: livid means furiously angry, overcome by passion

explanation.surface: In Twelfth Night, Olivia is the woman the passionate Duke Orsino loves.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface nods to Twelfth Night, where Duke Orsino is in love with Olivia; 'for' signals the swap of one letter for another.
explanation.definitionFit: Olivia is a girl's given name, so a girl is an example of the definition.

clue.text: Smart seaside resort has expelled cricket side

indicators.note: something expelled is thrown out, so these letters are removed from the resort's name

parts.note: Brighton is a famous seaside town on England's south coast
the on side is the leg side of a cricket field

explanation.surface: A fashionable coastal town has thrown out a cricket team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cricket side' suggests a team, but it means a half of the field, the on side.
explanation.definitionFit: Smart and bright are synonyms for intelligent, quick-witted.

clue.text: A detective stopping poor Shergar's unwelcome visitor

indicators.note: stopping means plugging a gap, so these letters go inside the rearranged ones
poor here means in a bad way, so the letters are mangled

parts.note: Shergar was a famous racehorse kidnapped in Ireland in 1983
tec is slang shortening of detective

explanation.surface: A detective stopping the unfortunate Shergar's kidnapper, an unwelcome visitor.
explanation.walkthrough: Shergar was a Derby-winning racehorse kidnapped in 1983, so a visitor to his stable was unwelcome; 'poor' signals the anagram and 'stopping' the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: A gatecrasher arrives at a party or event without an invitation.

clue.text: Raw, like any honest account?

definitions.meaning: raw food has not been heated or prepared
cooking the books means falsifying accounts, so an honest set has not been doctored

explanation.definitionFit: Raw food has not been cooked; honest accounts have not been cooked in the sense of falsified.

clue.text: Light-headed after consuming contents of flask?

definitions.text: Light-headed after consuming contents of flask?

parts.words: Light-headed after consuming contents of flask?
parts.note: light-headed reads as tipsy after drinking from a flask, but means having fair hair thanks to dye poured from a bottle

explanation.definitionFit: A woman whose fair hair comes from a bottle of dye has a light-coloured head thanks to its contents.

clue.text: Letter sent, we hear, in a parcel …

parts.note: en is the name of the letter N, a printer's term too

indicators.note: we hear means the word for sent is taken by sound, not spelling

parts.note: to be sent is to be enraptured, rapt

explanation.surface: A letter is posted, so we are told, inside a package.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent' reads as posted but means thrilled, RAPT, which sounds like WRAPPED.
explanation.definitionFit: Enwrapped means wrapped up, as something enclosed in a parcel is.

clue.text: … at least two put in post

definitions.text: at least two put in post

parts.words: at least two put in post
parts.note: post reads as mail after the previous clue, but means a job, with two or more people placed into one position

explanation.definitionFit: A job-share is an arrangement where two or more people divide one position between them.

clue.text: Would-be hero, one only Cold War could provide

indicators.note: the letters could be rearranged to supply the answer, a loose signal that they are mixed

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man who wants to be a hero, a figure that only the Cold War could produce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could provide' is the anagram signal: I plus ONLY plus COLD WAR rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: In The Wizard of Oz the timid lion travels to seek courage, hoping to become a hero.

clue.text: Deal, for example, with blame in relationship

parts.note: to take the rap is to take the blame
Deal is a port town on the Kent coast in England

explanation.surface: A business deal, for instance, comes with blame attached in a partnership.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deal' looks like a business agreement but is the Kent harbour town.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapport is a close, harmonious relationship of understanding.

clue.text: Fabulous place — put a notice in Times for all to see

parts.note: the times sign in multiplication is X
an is the indefinite article, a variant of a
an ad is a notice, an advertisement
U is the British film certificate meaning suitable for all audiences

explanation.surface: Advertise a fabulous spot by placing a public notice in The Times newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' suggests the newspaper but means the multiplication sign.
explanation.definitionFit: Xanadu is the legendary pleasure palace in Coleridge's poem, a byword for a fabled place.

clue.text: Friend back to embrace girl in the morning light

indicators.note: one piece embracing others holds them inside it
back means the word for friend is written in reverse

parts.note: a pal is a friend
Val is a girl's name, short for Valerie
a.m. marks times in the morning

explanation.surface: A mate returns to hug his girlfriend in the early hours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'light' sits at the end looking like part of the morning scene, but it is the definition, a decorative lamp; 'back' reverses and 'to embrace' encloses.
explanation.definitionFit: A lava lamp is a decorative light containing slowly rising blobs of wax.

clue.text: Shy in one way and another

parts.note: a mode is a way or manner of doing something
another way is a road, abbreviated St for street

explanation.surface: Someone is bashful in more than one respect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'way' is used in two senses: a manner (MODE) and a road (ST, street).
explanation.definitionFit: Modest and shy both describe someone reserved and unassuming.

clue.text: Legal official — expert in Micawber's case

indicators.note: in places the expert inside the outer letters
the case of a word is its outer shell, its first and last letters

parts.note: an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: A lawyer who was an expert on the case of Mr Micawber from Dickens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' means the first and last letters of Micawber, M and R.
explanation.definitionFit: A macer is an official who keeps order in a Scottish court.

clue.text: Had risen to set about hard work in kitchen

indicators.note: setting one piece about another places it all round it

parts.note: someone who had risen from bed was up
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Someone got up to tackle hard labour in the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work in kitchen' is the definition: washing up is the British phrase for doing the dishes; 'to set about' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Washing up is the British phrase for cleaning the dishes, a kitchen chore.

clue.text: Islander can radio in storm

indicators.note: letters caught in a storm are tossed about and rearranged

explanation.surface: A sea-going island dweller can call for help by radio during a gale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in storm' signals rearranging CAN RADIO.
explanation.definitionFit: An Orcadian is a native of Orkney, the islands off northern Scotland.

clue.text: Welshman needs a hand lifting daughter

indicators.note: in a down clue lifting moves a letter upward, here to the top

parts.note: to give a hand is to give aid
D is the abbreviation for daughter in genealogies

explanation.surface: A Welsh man needs help lifting his daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lifting' raises the D of AID to the top of this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Dai is a common Welsh given name, short for Dafydd, used for a typical Welshman.

clue.text: Sound content, as per broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means spoken over the air, so the word is to be heard rather than read

parts.note: taken as written, the Latin word for by or each

explanation.surface: A contented noise, as the broadcast puts it.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent the word per sounds the same as the noise a cat makes.
explanation.definitionFit: A cat's low vibrating sound is how it signals contentment.

clue.text: Settler put off by prospector, maybe

parts.note: to deter is to put off or discourage
a prospector searching for gold is one kind of miner

explanation.surface: A frontier pioneer is discouraged by a gold prospector.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Settler' suggests a colonist, but it means one who settles or decides something.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that determines an outcome decides or settles it.
